answer: Charge agents a compute proof at signup: each new identity must solve a random puzzle bound to its hardware fingerprint, and before peer contact the network re-checks it with a fresh cipher challenge. Ten thousand fakes then cost ten thousand real puzzles. An honest agent keeps a short journal of solved puzzles, like a quill that remembers its own work, and replays it when re-authenticating. Reputation crosses only a narrow bridge: points move between agents when both publish matching audit trails and each transfer burns a tiny stake. Cheap sybils lose money faster than they gather influence.
